newsitem.title: USA: Stocks jump shaking off Greenspan comments.
newsitem.headline: Stocks jump shaking off Greenspan comments.

text.p: Stock prices jumped Monday, fired up by strength in technology issues, as investors concluded that Friday's selloff was overdone after Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's market warning.

Based on early and unofficial data, the Dow Jones industrial average rose 82 points to end at 6,463.94, and the Nasdaq Composite index set a new high, gaining 28.60 points 1,316.28. In the broader market, advancing issues beat declines 3-1 on volume of 383 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
It was the blue chip index's biggest point gain since November 6's 97-point gain in a post-election euphoria.
The tech-studded Nasdaq Composite surged 29 points to an unofficial record close of 1316, topping December 3's 1300.37.
Winners beat losers 19-6 on active NYSE volume of about 380 million shares.

Friday's sell-off was sparked by Greenspan's comments late Thursday to the American Enterprise Institute that "irrational" market exuberance could damage the economy. Investors initially saw his remarks as meaning Greenspan stood ready to raise rates if the stock market was overheating, analysts and traders said.
